_comment: The CLI surface the stage table reads, and nothing else. Same design as the
regcf and sg-succession sidecars' pins: deliberately NOT a hash of
`l4 --help`, because any unrelated CLI change -- a new subcommand, a reworded
flag, a help reflow -- would fire a BROKEN verdict on an otherwise fine run,
and a tripwire that cries wolf gets deleted. These four enumerations and the
module's regulative rule names are the only CLI facts etc/go/phases/*.sh
depend on.
Recovered by probing, not by reading help text: `l4 <cmd> --help` answers
`Invalid option '--help'` for every subcommand, so a deliberately-bad enum
value whose error message lists the accepted set is the only discovery route
that exists. See etc/go/lib/discover.mjs.
MEASURED 2026-08-31 with `node etc/go/lib/discover.mjs enums
jl4/examples/legal/chubb/chubb.l4`, against the prebuilt binary at
l4wt/callgraph-materiality/dist-newstyle/build/aarch64-osx/ghc-9.10.3/jl4-0.1/x/l4/build/l4/l4
(sha256 c8d888b1d543c2f9...), with JL4_LIBRARY_PATH pointed at that
worktree's jl4-core/libraries. The four enumerations came back identical to
the ones regcf pinned on 2026-08-02 and sg-succession on 2026-08-18, which is
the expected result and is recorded rather than assumed.
`regulative_rules` IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY, and that is a fact about the
fixture rather than a gap in the measurement. Both the committed encoding and
the guarded-2026-08 arm are entirely CONSTITUTIVE: they decide whether a
claim survives every condition and exclusion the policy makes operative, and
they state no MUST, MAY or SHANT -- `grep -cE '\b(MUST|MAY|SHANT)\b'` returns
0 for each. `l4 export <module> --to bpmn` accordingly answers 'No regulative
rules found in module' for both, which discover.mjs treats as a legitimate
empty set rather than a shape change. p7-bpmn and p7-lts are therefore not
declared in subject.json; see its _comment for why, and NOTES.md for the one
clause (3.2.1, arbitration) that could become a regulative rule later. If it
does, this list and both legs change in one edit.
`checkers_that_must_exist` names ONE checker, and it is a standing guard
rather than a stage dependency: none of this subject's declared legs (p7-tnr,
p7-akn, p7-mcp) shells out to an etc/ checker at all. etc/check-not-precedence.mjs
is listed because both modules lean hard on NOT -- 27 occurrences in chubb.l4,
19 in chubb-denovo.l4 -- and NOT binds looser than AND in this grammar, a trap
that produced a WRONG LEGAL ANSWER in the sg-succession corpus rather than a
type error. Measured 2026-08-31: `node etc/check-not-precedence.mjs` over both
modules reports '2 file(s) clean'. Keeping the checker in the tree is what
makes that stay true.
